findings.title: Scrub mode, the default, lets 70 of 71 realistic credential command lines through to disk
findings.evidence: uv run python docs/review/probes/d-privacy/redact_leaks.py (rerun today, output identical): '84 cases, 71 of them not controls; 70 leaked in all'. Leaks per class: header 8/8 ('curl -H Authorization: Bearer FAKEtok...'), user:pass 10/10 ('curl -u alice:FAKEpw-7x', 'sshpass -p', 'docker login -p', 'sqlcmd -P', 'redis-cli -a', 'net use ... /user:'), attached short option 4/4 ('mysql -uroot -pFAKEpw-7x', '7z -p...'), opt=NAME=value 4/5 ('docker run --env=API_TOKEN=...', 'helm --set=auth.password=...'), slash options 6/6 ('cmdkey /pass:', 'schtasks /rp', 'xfreerdp /p:'), connection strings 6/6 ('Server=db;...;Password=...;', 'jdbc:...?user=alice&password=', 'redis://:pw@'), JSON 3/3, URLs 5/5 ('https://TOKEN@host', '?user=alice&token='), wrappers 10/10 ('bash -c "tool --api-key X"', 'cmd.exe /d /s /c', 'powershell -Command', 'wsl.exe -e bash -c'), provider shapes 7/7 (glpat-, rk_test_, SG., hvs., Telegram bot), secret names outside the list 7/7 (--auth, --key, --cookie, openssl -k, --pin). The only non-control hidden: 'kubectl create secret [redacted]'. Controls show the probe is wired right (e.g. 'docker run -e API_TOKEN=[redacted]', 'mysql --user root --password [redacted]'). Cause: redact.py:69-82 looks at one argument at a time; name-based hiding fires only for '-flag value' (redact.py:77) or NAME=value with the secret word before the first '=' (redact.py:74-76); the rest go to redact_text (redact.py:47-52): 5 token shapes plus scheme://user:pw@. tests/test_baseline.py:171-194 test exactly those handled forms. exe_only on the same 71 cases: 0 leaked (mode_tradeoff.out.txt). Attribution does not depend on the stored form: rules match the live, unredacted argv in memory (rules.py:84-86), attribution runs in the collector before storage (docs/17-build-prompt.md:52), and stored history is never re-attributed (docs/17:130). mode_tradeoff (rerun): 162 own processes with readable command lines; exe_only stores 97 distinct texts and scrub stores 150.
findings.impact: Credentials stay in raw/*.db for 48 h and are served by GET /workloads/{id}/processes and the dashboard process tree. The promise 'Command lines are scrubbed of secrets before they are stored' (docs/04-features.md:43) and the R04 fix are false for the way agents and developer tools actually pass credentials.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17-build-prompt.md:146, docs/08-configuration.md:104 and docs/04-features.md:43: make exe_only the default. Describe scrub as opt-in and best-effort ('hides known shapes; it cannot recognise every credential'). Change the default in src/submeter/core/config.py:186 and in the RawFile/RawStore defaults (raw.py:64, 247). Keep the cases from redact_leaks.py as a regression test that records which forms scrub is known to miss.
findings.cost: Three sentences in three documents, plus a one-word default in two files and a test
findings.decision_question: Default redaction: keep scrub (best-effort; 70 of 71 realistic credential command lines leaked here) or switch to exe_only (0 leaked from split argv; costs detail in the process drill-down, not attribution numbers)? Recommendation: exe_only by default, with scrub opt-in and documented as best-effort.
findings.refutation_attempt: Checked R04, docs/14-baseline-modules.md:189-194 and the tests for a stated limit: none. Re-ran the probe today with identical output. Checked whether attribution needs stored arguments: it does not (rules.py:84-86 uses the in-memory argv).

findings.title: exe_only mode stores the whole command line when a process's argv is one string
findings.evidence: redact.py:64-65: 'if mode == "exe_only": return (args[0],)'. unsplit_cmdlines.py (rerun): 'processes with a readable command line: 295 / of those, one string with spaces when split on NUL only: 64 / programs: .postgres-wrapp x31, chrome x17, ... / returned whole and unchanged in exe_only mode: 64'. These are processes that rewrite their own title (setproctitle), so /proc/PID/cmdline is one string. store_bytes.out.txt under 'redaction = exe_only': 'ON DISK  one unsplit string', 'ON DISK  rewritten title, unsplit'. psutil_provider.py:69 passes process.cmdline() through without splitting.
findings.impact: The strict mode, which is the documented answer to secret leaks ('a strict mode that stores the executable only', docs/17:146; docs/08:104), stores full titles for about a fifth of the processes on this machine. Postgres titles, for example, carry the user, the database and the client address. If F1 makes exe_only the default, this is the remaining leak.
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/privacy/redact.py:64-65 or src/submeter/store/raw.py:153-154: in exe_only mode store sample.exe (process.name()), never args[0]. In scrub mode, split an argv[0] that contains spaces on whitespace before scrubbing. Add a test with ('postgres: alice appdb 10.0.0.5(5432) idle',).
findings.refutation_attempt: Looked for splitting in the provider and the sampler: there is none. Re-ran the probe today: 64 again. Whether Windows ever returns an unsplit string is unknown, because psutil splits in C (_pswindows.py:763-775 calls cext.proc_cmdline), but the Linux case is enough to break the promise.

findings.title: One process with a non-UTF-8 argument stops every raw write while it lives
findings.lens: D privacy (storage robustness, any local user can trigger it)
findings.evidence: New probe: uv run python docs/review/probes/d-privacy/nonutf8_cmdline.py. 'psutil gives the child's last argument as: 'caf\udce9-FAKE'' then 'tick 1: FAILED with UnicodeEncodeError; workload rows in the file so far: 0' for ticks 1 to 3. Control with the same child left out: 'tick 3: written; workload rows in the file so far: 9'. Mechanism: RawFile.write runs the whole tick in one transaction (raw.py:96). _register binds the joined text (raw.py:154-155), and sqlite3 cannot encode a lone surrogate, so system_raw, workload_raw and the process rows are all rolled back. Because self._memory never records the key (raw.py:132-133), every later tick retries the registration and fails again. On Linux, other users' command lines are read too (other_users.out.txt: 104 such processes with arguments).
findings.impact: Any local process, including one owned by another user, can blind the collector: no samples and no gap row while it runs, so attribution, live diagnosis and trends all lose that period without a trace. A Latin-1 filename in an argument is enough.
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/store/raw.py _register: text = text.encode('utf-8', 'backslashreplace').decode('utf-8'), and the same for sample.exe and the workload name (or do it once in the provider). Add a test with a b'caf\xe9' argument. docs/17-build-prompt.md Operations: 'A record that cannot be stored is replaced by a marker; it never fails the tick.'
findings.cost: 3 lines plus a test and one sentence
findings.refutation_attempt: The control run, which leaves out only that child, writes normally. Pydantic accepts the surrogate; the failure is at the SQLite bind. No R-number covers it. Windows behaviour with unpaired UTF-16 surrogates is not checked.

findings.title: privacy.redact_patterns is never applied, and an invalid pattern passes validation and then raises at write time
findings.evidence: core/config.py:185-187: 'redact_patterns: tuple[str, ...] = ()' with no validator. grep shows no other use of redact_patterns in src. raw.py:154 calls redact_cmdline(sample.cmdline, mode=self._redaction) without extra patterns, and RawFile and RawStore (raw.py:58-65, 240-248) take no pattern argument. redact_side_effects.out.txt: 'RawStore accepts: files, keyframe_interval_s, cpu_points, memory_step, redaction', 'load_settings accepted the pattern '('', 'redact_cmdline then raised PatternError: missing ), unterminated subpattern at position 0'. Extra patterns run per argument (redact.py:81), so none can span a flag and its value. redact.py:66 compiles them on every call.
findings.impact: The documented control 'Add your own secret formats' (docs/08:105) does nothing. Wired up naively, a single typo raises inside the write transaction and, as in F3, makes every tick fail.
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/core/config.py Privacy: a field_validator that compiles each pattern and names the bad one. src/submeter/store/raw.py: RawFile and RawStore take redact_patterns, compile them once in __init__, and pass them at line 154. Add a test.
findings.refutation_attempt: Grepped src for any other path that reads the setting: none. Phase 1 may be meant to wire it, but the baseline interface (RawStore) has no way to take it, and the brief says to keep interfaces.

findings.title: Logs, validation errors, reprs and event rows bypass the store's redaction
findings.evidence: (a) redact_text is the only redaction that fits a log line, and it misses flag/value pairs, NAME=value, headers and query tokens. redact_side_effects.out.txt: 'LEAK launch failed: tool --api-key FAKEtok...', 'LEAK environment: API_TOKEN=FAKEtok...', 'LEAK upstream said 401 for Authorization: Bearer FAKEtok...', 'LEAK 127.0.0.1 "GET /api/v1/live?token=FAKEtok... HTTP/1.1" 101', 'LEAK could not read ['mysql', '--password', 'FAKEpw-7x']'. Yet docs/17:137 and docs/06-storage.md:19 promise logs 'with the same redaction as the store'. (b) Pydantic errors carry the input. error_values.out.txt: 'command line given as one string: str(error) contains the secret: True ... input_value='tool.exe --api-key FAKEsecret-9q''; with a missing field, str(error) shows the last five characters ('...cret-9q''). Pydantic docs: hide_input_in_errors 'Whether to hide inputs when printing errors. Defaults to False.' (https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/api/pydantic/config/). models.py:17 sets only extra and frozen. (c) repr(ProcessCounters) contains the raw argv: a one-liner printed 'repr shows the secret: True'. (d) record_event stores detail as given (raw.py:190-193); store_bytes shows 'ON DISK  event detail' in both modes. Not a leak: Typer 0.29.2 shows no locals by default (error_output.out.txt; Typer 0.23.0 release note: 'default to not showing locals').
findings.impact: Any log line built from a record, an exception message or a provider error carries the unredacted command line into logs/*.log (25 MB kept) or into event rows, even in exe_only mode.
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/core/models.py:17: add hide_input_in_errors=True. Mark cmdline and cwd Field(repr=False) at models.py:75-76 and 109-110. docs/17:137 and docs/06:19: replace 'with the same redaction as the store' with 'logs never contain command lines, working folders or the token: they name a process by pid and executable, and validation errors are logged without input values'. Event details are structured fields, never free text taken from a process.
findings.cost: About 6 lines in models.py and two sentences
findings.refutation_attempt: Checked whether Typer prints locals (it does not), whether hide_input_in_errors covers errors() (it does not; include_input=False is needed: error_values.out.txt), and whether any document already forbids command lines in logs: none.

findings.title: Scrub hides harmless arguments, and cmdline rules are written against text the user never sees
findings.evidence: over_redaction.out.txt shows these hidden: 'containerd-shim-runc-v2 -namespace moby -id [redacted]', 'claude --resume [redacted]', 'python [redacted]' (a 42-character script path without an extension), 'git -C [redacted] status', 'optimizer --passes [redacted] model.onnx', 'bazel build --bypass-cache [redacted]', 'psql --no-password-prompt [redacted]', 'env PWD=[redacted] make -j8'. redact_side_effects.out.txt also hides 'trainer --tokenizer', 'tool --token-limit', 'rg --passthru', 'git checkout <sha>' and 'cc1 <path> main.c'. Causes: _OPAQUE (redact.py:36) hides any run of 32 or more [A-Za-z0-9+/_=-] characters with a letter and a digit, which covers POSIX paths, UUIDs, container ids and commit hashes. _SECRET_NAME (redact.py:21-25) is an unanchored substring search, so 'pass' matches --passes and --passthru, and 'token(?!s)' matches --tokenizer. Part 2 of the probe: 'the collector matches rules against: python /home/alice/work/agents/refactor2/run_worker --queue nightly / the store, and so the process tree, shows: python [redacted] --queue nightly / a rule written from the shown text matches: False'.
findings.impact: The process drill-down loses the arguments that tell agent sessions, containers and checkouts apart, which hurts live diagnosis. A user who writes a cmdline rule from what the dashboard shows gets a rule that never matches, so the CPU stays Unattributed.
findings.proposed_change: If scrub is kept (see F1): in src/submeter/privacy/redact.py, anchor _SECRET_NAME to whole words of the flag (bounded by start, '-', '_' or end) and exempt strings that contain a path separator, or have UUID shape, from _OPAQUE; add tests. In docs/17 Interfaces, state that cmdline rules match the unredacted live command line and that `submeter rules test` reads the live process, marking which arguments the store hides.
findings.cost: About 6 lines in redact.py plus tests, and one sentence
findings.refutation_attempt: docs/14:192 accepts over-hiding of commit hashes, but nothing accepts hiding script paths, session ids or ordinary flags. Checked that Windows paths survive ('C:\src\...' is kept because of ':' and '\'), so this is mainly a POSIX problem.

findings.title: Folders and data files are created readable by everyone (0755/0644), against 'restrict every data file and the API token to the current user'
findings.evidence: file_modes.out.txt, temporary SUBMETER_HOME, umask 0022: 'dir 0755 readable by owner, group, everyone data' (also raw, minute, runs, settings, state, logs), 'file 0644 ... data/raw/2026-11-20.db' with -wal and -shm, 'file 0644 ... state/collector.pid'. Only collector.lock is 0600 (files.py:222). Code: files.py:119 folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); raw.py:68 sqlite3.connect creates the file with SQLite's default mode; files.py:230 writes the pid file with write_text; the docstring at files.py:204 says the pid file is one 'which anyone may read'. The fix works on POSIX: private_files.out.txt 'folders: home 0700, data 0700, raw 0700 / database 0600, side files made by SQLite: {'-shm': '0600', '-wal': '0600'} / token 0600, pid file 0600 / backup into a new file 0644, into a file made first 0600'. Mitigation here: the home folder is 0750, but SUBMETER_HOME (files.py:48-51) can point anywhere. Windows: Python docs for os.mkdir say 'On Windows, a mode of 0o700 is specifically handled to apply access control to the new directory such that only the current user and administrators have access. Other values of mode are ignored.' and 'Changed in version 3.12.4: Windows now handles a mode of 0o700.' (https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/os.html#os.mkdir). pyproject.toml:5 allows '>=3.12'. Path.mkdir with parents: 'they are created with the default permissions without taking mode into account' (https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html). Microsoft: 'If you specify NULL for the lpSecurityAttributes parameter, the file or directory gets a default security descriptor. The ACLs in the default security descriptor for a file or directory are inherited from its parent directory.' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/file-security-and-access-rights).
findings.impact: On a shared Linux machine, or with SUBMETER_HOME outside a private folder, other users can read command lines and history. A token file written the same way would give them the whole API, since loopback is shared by all users. On Windows the protection is whatever the parent folder grants, which under a SUBMETER_HOME on another drive is unknown.
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/store/files.py ensure(): create each level under the Submeter root with os.mkdir(path, 0o700), not parents=True, and chmod existing levels to 0o700 on POSIX. src/submeter/store/raw.py (and later stores): os.open(path, O_CREAT|O_RDWR, 0o600) before sqlite3.connect; the probe shows -wal and -shm inherit 0600. The InstanceLock pid file and the token: os.open(..., O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY, 0o600). Backups go into a file made 0600 first. pyproject.toml: requires-python '>=3.12.4'. doctor flags any Submeter path readable by others. Add tests under umask 0022.
findings.cost: About 25 lines in files.py and raw.py, tests, and one line in pyproject
findings.refutation_attempt: R30 states the requirement ('a token file only you can read') but the baseline does not meet it for data files. Ran under umasks 0002, 0022 and 0077: only 0077 gives private files. The Windows ACL of a folder made under %LOCALAPPDATA% or on a drive root was not checked (win_confirm.py check 1).

findings.title: How each client carries the token is unspecified, and the brief's rules push the token into URLs, logs and command lines
findings.evidence: docs/17:148 says only 'Require a token on every HTTP and WebSocket request ... and check Origin on the WebSocket'; no document names a transport (grep for cookie, subprotocol, query and CSP finds nothing). A browser WebSocket cannot send headers: MDN lists only 'new WebSocket(url)' and 'new WebSocket(url, protocols)' (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebSocket/WebSocket). Opening the dashboard cannot carry a header either, so 'every HTTP request' leaves a URL token or a cookie. A URL token is logged: uvicorn defaults to access_log: bool = True with access format '%(client_addr)s - "%(request_line)s" %(status_code)s', and get_path_with_query_string appends '?' plus the query string (github.com/encode/uvicorn master, uvicorn/config.py and uvicorn/protocols/utils.py). Submeter's own redaction misses it: 'LEAK url chrome http://127.0.0.1:8787/?range=1h&token=FAKEtok...' (redact_leaks), and it is hidden only when token is the first key. Python's webbrowser puts the URL on the browser's command line (stdlib webbrowser.py:190-196, 'cmdline = [self.name] + [arg.replace("%s", url) ...]; subprocess.Popen(cmdline)'), and other Linux users can read browser command lines (other_users.out.txt). A cookie is no better: RFC 6265 section 8.5 says 'Cookies do not provide isolation by port.' (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6265.html), so every other loopback dev server receives it, and a page from another localhost port could POST /sessions unless Origin is checked on HTTP too. The documents disagree on that: docs/17:148 checks Origin on the WebSocket only, while docs/17:272 and docs/15:25 refuse 'a foreign Origin' on all requests. The MCP spec says 'Servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks' (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/transports). Also unspecified: whether the served HTML may embed the token (any local user can fetch it over shared loopback), how MCP gets the token (redact_leaks: 'LEAK header npx mcp-remote https://... --header Authorization: Bearer FAKE...' is the common bridge, and Submeter records it), and what rotate-token does to open WebSockets.
findings.impact: Depending on how it is built, the token ends up in access logs, browser history, the browser's command line (readable by other Linux users and stored by Submeter's own collector), or a cookie sent to every localhost port. The phase-4 gate passes in every one of these designs.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17-build-prompt.md, 'Privacy and local security', add: 'The CLI and MCP send the token in an Authorization header, read from the token file. The dashboard shell (HTML, JS, CSS) is served without a token and never contains one. The CLI opens it with the token in the URL fragment (#t=...), which the page moves to sessionStorage and strips with history.replaceState. API calls use the Authorization header; the WebSocket sends the token as its first message and is closed if no valid token arrives within 2 s. No cookies. A token in a query string is refused. Host and Origin are checked on every HTTP, WebSocket and MCP request. Access logs omit query strings. rotate-token closes every open WebSocket and MCP session.' Phase-4 gate: the test run's logs and raw files do not contain the token.
findings.cost: One paragraph and one gate clause in docs/17
findings.refutation_attempt: Searched docs for any transport, cookie or CSP statement: none. R04's fix names only 'token' and 'Host and Origin headers'. FastAPI, uvicorn and Starlette are not installed in .venv, so uvicorn behaviour comes from its source on GitHub, not from a run.

findings.title: Clients send the token to whatever holds the port, and the default 8787 is Cloudflare Wrangler's default dev port
findings.evidence: port_first.out.txt: 'the client was answered: 200 {"status":"ok"} / the stand-in, which is not Submeter, received: ['Authorization: Bearer FAKE-api-token'] / a server starting afterwards cannot bind the port: Address already in use'. localhost_split.out.txt: 'a second program bound [::1] on the same port while 127.0.0.1 was held: True' (localhost resolves only to 127.0.0.1 on this machine). Default port: docs/08:107 '8787', config.py:197 'port: int = Field(default=8787, ...)'. Cloudflare's Wrangler configuration docs: 'port: Port for the local dev server to listen on. Defaults to 8787.' and 'ip: IP address for the local dev server to listen on. Defaults to localhost.' (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/configuration/). Loopback ports are shared by all OS users, so another user can hold the port while Submeter's server is down (logon, crash, restart).
findings.impact: With wrangler dev running, Submeter's server cannot start, and the CLI and MCP send the token to the user's Worker and show its answers. On a shared machine a squatter collects the token or serves made-up numbers to the CLI and to agents. Nothing in the brief detects either case.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17 'Privacy and local security': 'After binding, the server writes state/api.json (port, pid, start time, mode 0600). Clients take the port from it, connect to the literal 127.0.0.1 (never "localhost"), and before sending the token confirm that the listener is that pid, or have the server answer a challenge with HMAC(token, nonce). If the port is taken, the server refuses to start and names the holder.' docs/08:107 and config.py:197: choose a default not used by common dev servers, or 0 (ephemeral, written to api.json).
findings.cost: Three sentences and one default value
findings.refutation_attempt: A same-user squatter gains nothing, because it can read the token file anyway, so the finding rests on other users and on harmless collisions. Searched docs for port-in-use handling: none. Windows localhost order and SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE behaviour were not checked (win_confirm.py checks 3 and 4).

findings.title: 'MCP never returns command lines' is a courtesy, not a boundary, and the documents disagree on what MCP withholds
findings.evidence: docs/17:148: 'The MCP server must never return command lines or working directories'. docs/17:193, docs/08-configuration.md:125 and docs/05-data-flow.md:50 mention command lines only, and the gate at docs/17:274 tests only 'no MCP response contains a command line'. The agent runs as the same user (fixed rule 2), so it can read raw/*.db (the command table, raw.py:36) and the token file (files.py:96-97) directly. MCP spec: 'The client launches the MCP server as a subprocess.' (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/transports). Findings carry 'the evidence that triggered them' (docs/17:152) with no rule against command lines, and findings are kept forever in history.db (docs/06:15), outside the 48 h raw retention that R25 relies on. MCP tool results go into the agent's context, which a hosted agent sends to its model provider (inference, not vendor-verified). That is the designed path by which Submeter data leaves the machine.
findings.impact: Readers will treat the MCP rule as a security boundary, which it is not. Working directories may be returned, since no gate tests for them. Command lines can reach history (kept forever) and MCP through findings evidence.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17:148 and docs/08:125: 'The MCP server returns workload names, numbers, findings and verdicts only: never command lines, working folders, executable paths or the token. This limits what reaches an agent's context, and so what its model provider receives; it does not stop an agent running as the same user from reading the data files.' docs/17 Analysis: 'Evidence names workloads, executables and metrics, never a command line.' Gate at docs/17:274: 'no MCP response contains a stored command line, a working folder or the token'.
findings.refutation_attempt: Checked whether any document scopes the MCP rule as a boundary against the local user: none. Checked whether evidence is defined anywhere (docs/07-analysis.md): its content is not restricted.

findings.title: The named stack and the dashboard mock make the browser contact other hosts by default (fixed rule 3)
findings.evidence: FastAPI (named in docs/17:38): 'By default, those files are served from a CDN.' and 'The first step is to disable the automatic docs, as by default, those use the default CDN.', with the defaults https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/swagger-ui-dist@5/swagger-ui-bundle.js and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/redoc@2/bundles/redoc.standalone.js (https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/how-to/custom-docs-ui-assets/). So a default app serves /docs and /redoc pages that fetch from jsDelivr. docs/brief.html:7-9 loads https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=IBM+Plex+Mono... on open (mock_scan.out.txt 'fetched when the page opens'). docs/17:39 'Use a canvas chart library such as uPlot' does not say it must be served locally, and 'Self-contained HTML reports' (docs/04:37) is not defined as having no external references. uv docs: 'when uv run is used, the project is locked and synced before invoking the requested command.' (https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/sync/). The brief does not say what the logon task or unit runs; uv_run_network.out.txt shows 0 connect() calls in an environment that is already synced. The baseline itself opens 0 sockets (no_network.out.txt).
findings.impact: In a default build, opening /docs or /redoc, or a dashboard that copies the mock's font links or a CDN chart library, makes the user's browser contact jsDelivr or Google: rule 3 is broken by default, before any user setting. A logon task that runs `uv run` contacts the package index whenever the lock or cache changed.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17-build-prompt.md 'Stack and conventions': 'Create the FastAPI app with docs_url=None, redoc_url=None and openapi_url=None. Every script, style, font and image the dashboard and reports use ships in the package and is served by the server; no page references another host. The dashboard sends Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; reports carry a meta CSP default-src 'none' with hashes for their inline code. The scheduled task and the systemd unit run the installed entry point, not uv run.' Add a test that fails on any http(s):// reference in the built front end or a report.
findings.refutation_attempt: Checked the docs for a vendoring or CSP rule: none. Severity is critical because the fixed rule breaks in a default build, though it needs a user to open /docs or a design that copies the mock; the lead may grade it as high.

findings.title: R05's 'ingest API' for the WSL guest collector conflicts with the loopback-only, read-only API, and default WSL networking cannot reach host loopback
findings.evidence: docs/16-review-log.md:81 (R05 fix): 'The ingest API accepts a second collector, so the Linux build can run inside WSL and report to the host.' docs/17:79: 'Design the ingest path so a second collector running inside the guest can report to the host later (phase 7)'. docs/17:254: the API is 'read-only except session markers'. docs/13-build-list.md:69-83 lists no ingest route, and docs/13:5 says the programs 'share only files on disk'. Microsoft: 'By default, WSL uses a NAT (Network Address Translation) based architecture'; 'If you want to access a networking app running on Windows ... from your Linux distribution (ie Ubuntu), then you need to use the IP address of your host machine.'; 'you may need to bind your application to 0.0.0.0 instead of 127.0.0.1'. Mirrored mode (Windows 11 22H2 and later, opt-in through .wslconfig) lets you 'Connect to Windows servers from within Linux using the localhost address 127.0.0.1' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/networking).
findings.impact: Phase 7 as written either binds beyond loopback (breaking fixed rule 3) under default WSL, depends on the user changing a WSL setting, or adds a write route the brief says does not exist and gives the token to a guest VM. Phase 7 may move to right after phase 2.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17:79 and the R05 fix text in docs/16: 'The guest collector writes its own raw files into the host's data folder through the Windows file system (/mnt/c/...); the server reads them like any raw file. There is no network path and no ingest route.'
findings.decision_question: Guest collector transport: raw files written through /mnt/c (keeps the files-only contract and loopback-only binding) or the loopback API under mirrored networking (needs Windows 11 22H2 or later and a .wslconfig change, adds a write route, and hands the guest the token)? Recommendation: files through /mnt/c.
findings.refutation_attempt: Looked for an ingest route or a transport anywhere in docs/13, docs/15 and docs/17: none. Mirrored mode is opt-in, so it cannot be assumed.

findings.title: daemon install's scheduled task may need administrator rights (fixed rule 2)
findings.evidence: docs/17:199: '`submeter daemon start|stop|status|install|uninstall`, installing a Windows scheduled task at logon'. Microsoft schtasks create: 'The /ru parameter determines the permissions under which the task runs, not the permissions used to schedule the task. Only Administrators can schedule tasks, regardless of the value of the /ru parameter.' and 'ONLOGON - Specifies that the task runs whenever a user (any user) logs on.' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/schtasks-create). That sentence sits in the System-account section, so the documentation does not settle whether a standard user can register a logon task for themselves. docs/15-phases-and-decisions.md:46 says admin rights are often unavailable on the target work computer.
findings.impact: If registration is refused, `daemon install` fails on the target machine or asks to elevate, which breaks fixed rule 2.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17:199: 'installing per-user autostart that needs no elevation: a scheduled task for the current user if phase 0 shows a standard user can register one, otherwise an entry under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run; a systemd user unit on Linux'. Add the check to the phase 0 gate.
findings.refutation_attempt: Read the whole schtasks create page: no sentence says a standard user may create a local logon task for themselves, and one says only Administrators can schedule tasks. Not run, because this machine is Linux.
findings.would_confirm: On Windows 11 as a standard user, not elevated: schtasks /create /tn SubmeterProbe /tr "cmd /c exit" /sc onlogon /ru %USERNAME% /it ; and powershell -c "Register-ScheduledTask -TaskName SubmeterProbe2 -Action (New-ScheduledTaskAction -Execute cmd.exe -Argument '/c exit') -Trigger (New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -AtLogOn -User $env:USERNAME)" ; record SUCCESS or 'Access is denied', then schtasks /delete /tn SubmeterProbe /f (and SubmeterProbe2).

findings.title: Forbidding breakaway may make programs run under `submeter run` fail to start children (fixed rule 1)
findings.evidence: docs/17:69: 'Set no limits on the group. Do not allow breakaway and do not set kill-on-close.' Microsoft, CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB: 'If the calling process is associated with a job, the job must set the JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK limit.' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/process-creation-flags). JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK: 'If any process associated with the job creates a child process using the CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB flag while this limit is in effect, the child process is not associated with the job.' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winnt/ns-winnt-jobobject_basic_limit_information). The documentation states the requirement but not what happens without it.
findings.impact: If CreateProcess fails without the limit, a command behaves differently under `submeter run` than without it: Submeter changes a process's behaviour, against the intent of fixed rule 1, and the user blames their own tool.
findings.proposed_change: docs/17:69: either allow breakaway (JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_BREAKAWAY_OK, so behaviour is unchanged; a child that breaks away is polled and the run reports it), or keep the ban and list it in docs/10-known-limits.md. Add a test to the phase 2 gate.
findings.decision_question: Allow breakaway (no behaviour change; children that break away fall back to polling) or forbid it (exact totals, but such spawns may fail)? Recommendation: allow it with BREAKAWAY_OK and report breakaway children, because fixed rule 1 outranks accounting precision.
findings.refutation_attempt: Checked whether docs/17:23 counts placing a tree in a job as allowed: it does, but only when no limit is set. Not checked whether the absent limit makes CreateProcess fail.
findings.would_confirm: On Windows, not elevated: uv run python docs/review/probes/d-privacy/win_confirm.py. Check 2 prints 'inside it, a breakaway spawn failed: ...' or 'succeeded'.

findings.title: The lock's pid file outlives its holder, so a pid-based `daemon stop` could signal an unrelated process (fixed rule 1)
findings.evidence: stale_pid.out.txt: 'child took the lock: True; holder() names the child: True / after the child was killed, holder() still names it: True / a process with that pid exists now: False / the pid file holds only: '<pid>' (no start time) / the lock itself is free again: True'. files.py:229-230 writes only os.getpid(), holder() (files.py:233-238) returns it unchecked, and only release() deletes it (files.py:243-244), which a crash skips. How docs/17:199 `daemon stop` finds its target is unspecified.
findings.impact: Pids are reused. After a crash, a stop built as 'signal holder()' can end an unrelated process of the user, which breaks observe-only.
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/store/files.py: write 'pid create_time' to the pid file, and have holder() return None unless the lock is really held (a non-blocking probe of the lock) and the live process's create time matches. docs/17 Operations: '`daemon stop` asks the program to exit (an API call, a stop file or the service manager) and never signals a pid it has not verified.'
findings.cost: About 10 lines plus a test, and one sentence
findings.refutation_attempt: Read docs/14:281 and the InstanceLock docstring: both call the pid 'a convenience', but it is the only handle the baseline offers for finding the running program.

findings.title: Workload names are not validated: reserved names can be claimed, and HTML or paths pass through
findings.evidence: workload_names.out.txt: 'accepted: rule with workload = 'system'', and likewise for 'restricted', 'unattributed', 'submeter', 'machine', '', 'a\nb', '../../x', '' and a 300-character name. 'workload 'system': 0.5 CPU-s from 1 process' (a user rule for exe 'miner') and 'workload 'submeter': 0.5 CPU-s from 1 process' (a run tagged --as submeter). rules.py:56 'workload: str' has no constraint, the reserved names are at rules.py:34-37, and aggregate merges by name (rules.py:205). docs/brief.html lines 5418, 5423, 5428 and 5508 put w.name into innerHTML unescaped (mock_scan.out.txt).
findings.impact: A natural rule such as workload = "system" for svchost or systemd folds user processes into the System row. Tagging --as submeter inflates Submeter's own overhead, which feeds the overhead_fraction alert (docs/17:186). Unchecked names also reach Job Object and cgroup names, run files and, if the mock's pattern is copied, dashboard HTML.
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/core: one WorkloadName type, ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._:-]{0,63}$, that refuses the five reserved names unless the attributor assigns them itself. Use it for Rule.workload, AlertRule workload patterns and `submeter run --as`. docs/17 Dashboard: 'Insert text from data with textContent, never innerHTML.' Add a test.
findings.cost: About 10 lines plus a test, and one sentence
findings.refutation_attempt: R29 limits how many names exist, not which ones. Checked for a validator on Rule: there is only _usable (rules.py:65-74), which checks conditions, not the name.

findings.title: On Linux the collector stores other users' command lines
findings.evidence: other_users.py (rerun): 'processes in one snapshot: 454 / owned by another user (kernel threads included): 292 / of those, handed to the store with arguments in the command line: 104 / belonging to root: 55; distinct other owners: 12 / marked restricted by the provider: 104'. psutil_provider.py:67-71 reads cmdline whoever the owner is.
findings.impact: Submeter copies other accounts' command lines, including secrets that scrub misses (F1), into this user's files, which are readable by everyone by default (F7).
findings.proposed_change: src/submeter/providers/psutil_provider.py and the phase-1 /proc reader: for processes owned by another uid, keep exe only (cmdline=None, cwd=None). Add one sentence to docs/17 Privacy.
findings.refutation_attempt: Moot once exe_only becomes the default (F1), apart from F2's unsplit titles. Windows standard users cannot read other users' command lines, so this applies to Linux only.

Typer 0.29.2 tracebacks: no local variables by default, since the baseline app does not set pretty_exceptions_show_locals (error_output.out.txt; Typer 0.23.0 changelog)

Working folders are never stored: there is no cwd column in the raw schema (raw.py:33-54; store_bytes 'absent working folder')
CLI --json output in the baseline: top prints workload totals and doctor prints folder paths; no command lines

measurements: redact_leaks: 84 cases, 71 non-control, 70 leaked in scrub; exe_only 0/71 leaked (split argv). Unsplit argv: 64 of 295 readable cmdlines (postgres x31, chrome x17), all 64 stored whole in both modes. Own processes: 162 readable; distinct stored texts exe_only 97 vs scrub 150; scrub hides at least one argument in 38. Other users: 292 of 454 processes; 104 with arguments sent to the store (55 root, 12 owners). Non-UTF-8 argv: 3 of 3 ticks failed (0 workload rows) vs control 9 rows. File modes at umask 0022: dirs 0755, db/-wal/-shm 0644, pid 0644, lock 0600; proposed fix gives 0700/0600, and SQLite side files inherit 0600.
